- **Document ID:** E084
- **Brand/Company:** Network Rail (UK national railway)
- **Industry:** Rail/Transportation
- **Year:** 2022 (September)
- **File Size:** 0.3 MB
- **Page Count:** 30

- **Software:** Adobe InDesign 17.0
- **Format:** A4 landscape (841.89 x 595.276 pts)
- **Authors:** Anthony Dewar (Technical Head Buildings & Architecture), Frank Anatole (Principal Architect)
- **Symbol Designer:** Nick Job (with Design Council), refining original 1964 design by Gerry Barney (DRU)

## Brand Strategy
This document is narrowly scoped: it is a design manual exclusively for "Rail Symbol 2," the redesigned British Rail double-arrow symbol. The symbol is described as "a powerful visual statement of the intention for the British railway network to function effectively and efficiently as a cohesive and unified whole." Following the Williams-Shapps Plan for Rail (May 2021), the original 1965 symbol was carefully redrawn to meet modern digital standards while maintaining its heritage. This is not a full brand guidelines document but a single-asset specification manual within a broader document suite (100-400 series covering Strategic Planning, Design, Compliance, Operational Property).

## Logo
- **Rail Symbol 2:** The iconic British Rail "double arrow" -- two-way traffic arrows on parallel lines representing tracks.
- **Redesign rationale:** Original had 38:23 proportions and two optical variants (positive/negative). Redesign rationalizes to 8:5 proportions (near golden ratio), reduces to a single variant, and adjusts arms for better small-size/low-resolution performance.
- **Construction:** Detailed grid drawing with precise proportional measurements. Point-to-point dimensions are precisely square. Symbol is twice the height of the tracks.
- **Visual attributes:** Top arrow always points right (reflecting UK left-side running). Arms are flared for even thickness appearance. Track depth (A) < space between tracks (B) < space above/below tracks (C) in ratio 3:4:5.
- **Exclusion zone:** Defined as 1/4 W and 1/4 H around the symbol, resulting in a 1.5W x 1.5H total space.
- **Lozenge version:** Ruled rectangle version for station fascia signage, identifiers, projecting signs. Tighter margin (1/8 W and 1/8 H).
- **House flag:** 2:1 proportion (matching Union Flag). Five acceptable sizes from 2000x1000mm to 6000x3000mm depending on flagpole height.
- **Minimum size:** Print 4x2.5mm (300dpi+), absolute minimum 2x1.25mm. Digital: 32x20px minimum for full integrity, 16x10px absolute minimum.
- **Incorrect usage:** 24 specific examples across 4 categories: no mathematical transformations (reflect/rotate/stretch/shear), no dimension changes (parallel arms/lengthened tracks/weight changes), no combination with other elements (enclosing/strips/tracks/integration), no visual effects (perspective/3D/shadows/blur), no added complexity (outlines/contours/patterns/fills/multi-color), no overworking (repetition/patterns/textures/derivatives).

## Color
- **Red:** RAL 3020 Traffic Red / NCS S 1085-Y80R / CMYK 0,100,100,0 / Pantone 485 C / RGB 230,0,0 / HEX #E60000 / HSL H0 S100 L45.1 / 3M Scotchcal 100-13 / Avery 925 Signal Red
- **White:** RAL 9016 Traffic White / NCS S 0500-N / CMYK 0,0,0,0 / RGB 255,255,255 / HEX #FFFFFF / 3M Scotchcal 100-10 / Avery 900 White
- **Black:** RAL 9005 Jet Black / NCS S 9000-N / CMYK 0,0,0,100 / Pantone Black C / RGB 0,0,0 / HEX #000000 / 3M Scotchcal 100-12 / Avery 901 Black
- **Colourways:** Red or black on white; white reversed out of red or black; white on any other colored/photographic backgrounds (with sufficient contrast).

## Graphics / Visual Language
- **3D applications:** Permitted in architectural contexts against surfaces. Return depth up to track depth (ideal: 2/3 track depth). Laminar versions (e.g., stainless steel) may be raised from surface.
- **Low fidelity variants:** Dot matrix display versions at 32x20, 24x15, 16x10, 12x8, and 8x8 (square, last resort). Must maintain rotational symmetry and be unambiguously identifiable.

## Photography
Not covered. One historical photo of station lozenge signage is included as reference.

## Applications
- Station signage (fascia, totems, projecting wall signs)
- House flags (with specific size-to-flagpole-height relationships)
- Three-dimensional fabricated symbols (architectural)
- Dot matrix electronic indicators
- Digital media
- Print materials
- Vector assets provided: EPS and SVG in CMYK and RGB for all 5 configurations (red, black, white-on-red, white-on-black, lozenge).

## Tone of Voice
Not covered. The document itself is written in precise, formal, technical language appropriate for engineering/infrastructure standards.

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- This is a rare example of a single-symbol specification manual -- not a full brand guidelines document. Its scope is deliberately narrow and deep.
- The historical context is exceptional: tracing the symbol from Gerry Barney's 1964 design at DRU through to the 2022 digital optimization by Nick Job with the Design Council.
- Color specifications include RAL, NCS, Pantone, CMYK, RGB, HEX, HSL, and even specific 3M Scotchcal and Avery film references -- unusually thorough for physical material specification.
- The proportional redesign from 38:23 to 8:5 (near golden ratio) with detailed mathematical justification is technically rigorous.
- The document includes embedded vector artwork files (EPS/SVG) accessible via Adobe Acrobat.
- Part of Network Rail's broader document suite (NR/GN/CIV/300 series).
- Rail Symbol 2 is a registered trademark of the Department for Transport.
- Foreword by Sir Peter Hendy CBE, Chair of Network Rail.

## Quality Score
**5/5** -- An exemplary single-asset specification document. Extraordinarily thorough in its coverage of construction, proportions, exclusion zones, color specifications (across 8 color systems), minimum sizes for both print and digital, 3D fabrication guidelines, low-fidelity variants, and 24 specific incorrect usage examples. The historical context enriches the rationale. Color specs including RAL, NCS, and specific vinyl film references demonstrate real-world material awareness. The only limitation is its narrow scope (single symbol, not a full brand system), but within that scope it is near-perfect.
